subtopics.title: One Third of the Box — Volumes of Pyramids and Cones

questions.question: A cone or pyramid fills what fraction of the cylinder or prism sharing its base and height?
options: About one third, depending on the solid

questions.question: A square pyramid has base edge 12 cm and perpendicular height 8 cm. Its volume is:
A cone has radius 5 cm and perpendicular height 12 cm. Its exact volume is:
The height belonging in every volume formula is:
options: The slant height along the sloping side
The perpendicular height, apex straight down to the centre of the base

subtopics.title: Manufacturing the Slant Height with Pythagoras

questions.question: For the cone with r = 5 and h = 12, the slant height s is:
For a square pyramid, the horizontal leg of the slant-height triangle is:
options: Half the base edge — centre of base to midpoint of a side
The radius of the base circle

questions.question: The total surface area of a closed cone is:
The pyramid (edge 12, s = 10) has total surface area:
options: 384 cm² — base 144 plus four triangles of 60

subtopics.title: Sphere Formulas — the Power of r Remembers

questions.question: The two sphere formulas are:
A sphere has radius 3 cm. Its exact volume is:
A CLOSED hemisphere of radius 3 has surface area:
options: 27π — half the skin (18π) plus the new flat circle (9π)

questions.question: If you blank on which sphere formula is which, the reminder is:
options: The bigger number is the volume
Volume has the four, surface has the third
Cubed fills, squared wraps — the power of r matches the dimensions

subtopics.title: Glued Solids and the Buried-Face Audit

questions.question: The spinning top: cone (r = 3, h = 4) plus hemisphere (r = 3). Its total volume is:
options: 30π cm³ — volumes of glued solids simply add

questions.question: At the join of the spinning top, which faces are buried?
options: The cone's base circle and the hemisphere's flat circle

questions.question: The top's outside surface area (cone s = 5) is:
options: 33π cm² — curved cone 15π plus hemisphere skin 18π

questions.question: A cone volume computed WITHOUT the one third is:
options: Three times too big — it is the cylinder's answer
Out by a factor of pi

subtopics.title: A Party Hat, a Marquee and a Netball

questions.question: The pour test — cone filling its matching cylinder — takes exactly:
The marquee: square floor 12 by 12, height 8. Its volume is:
Why does the netball's volume formula cube the radius while its skin formula squares it?
options: Filling is three-dimensional, wrapping is two-dimensional — one power per dimension
Because the sphere has no edges

questions.question: The silo: cylinder (r = 2, h = 3) plus cone roof (r = 2, h = 1,5). The grain space is:
The roof's slant height (h = 1,5, r = 2) is:
The sheeting on the roof measures:
options: 5π m² — π times radius 2 times slant 2,5

questions.question: Which surface is NOT billed on the silo's outside?
options: The cone's base circle — it is the buried ceiling

subtopics.title: Four Traps — Heights, Hemispheres and Hidden Circles

questions.question: Perpendicular height and slant height belong, respectively, to:
Halving a sphere halves the volume. The surface of the closed half:
options: Is half the skin PLUS the newly exposed circle πr²
Stays equal to the full sphere's

questions.question: A dome resting on a building: does its flat circle join the surface bill?
options: Only if the dome is large
No — the rim is attached, not exposed; the story decides

questions.question: Your cone's volume equals the surrounding cylinder's volume. That signals:
options: The missing one third — the answer is three times too big
